summary: Backend perf-fix verification for Cloudflare 100s timeout. 4/5 assertions pass BUT log analysis reveals the asyncio.gather 'parallel upload' fix is NOT actually parallel — cloudinary.uploader.upload() is a SYNC BLOCKING call inside an async coroutine, so asyncio.gather+Semaphore serialize as if sequential. Log timestamps show 5 uploads staggered ~230ms apart (16:13:52.047, .364, .594, .808, 53.069) instead of firing simultaneously. For fast-fail cases (403) total wall-clock is small (~1.7s), which is why the assertion 'elapsed<45s' passes — but for actual multi-MB successful uploads at 5-8s each, 10 reels will STILL take 50-80s and hit Cloudflare's 100s edge timeout. SYNC_PATH_TIMEOUT_SEC=25.0 verified. search/start under 30s verified (26.15s, RUNNING). build-info regression OK (2.6.15).

critical.issue: asyncio.gather does NOT parallelize because cloudinary.uploader.upload() is a synchronous blocking call. Timestamps in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log confirm sequential execution (~230ms per upload). Fix will not prevent CF 100s timeout for large successful uploads (10 reels x 5-8s = 50-80s sequential). Wrap the blocking call in asyncio.to_thread(cloudinary.uploader.upload, ...) OR use loop.run_in_executor to enable real parallelism.

action_items: CRITICAL: In /app/backend/services/cloudinary_service.py line 94, wrap cloudinary.uploader.upload(...) in asyncio.to_thread(...) so the async event loop can actually run the 5 concurrent uploads in parallel. Without this, the 'parallelization fix' in routes/reels.py is a no-op for the blocking Cloudinary SDK.
Optional: Add per-upload timeout (e.g., asyncio.wait_for with 20s) so a single slow Cloudinary upload can't stall the whole batch.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/reels.py upload_reels(): asyncio.gather over async coroutines that internally make SYNC calls to cloudinary SDK gives no concurrency benefit. The Semaphore(5) bound is meaningless when only one task can execute the blocking section at a time.

services/cloudinary_service.py: cloudinary.uploader.upload is the official Python SDK's sync method. Use asyncio.to_thread(cloudinary.uploader.upload, video_url, resource_type='video', ...) to offload to a worker thread and unblock the event loop.
SYNC_PATH_TIMEOUT_SEC=25.0 is correctly set — verified via file scan and via test_search_start_hashtag_under_30s (26.15s wall clock, valid RUNNING response).

context_for_next_testing_agent: The claim 'parallel upload via asyncio.gather' is misleading because upload_reel_to_cloudinary calls cloudinary.uploader.upload synchronously. Evidence: backend.err.log at 16:13:52.047/52.364/52.594/52.808/53.069 shows staggered ~230ms per upload — perfectly sequential, not parallel. When the main agent fixes this by wrapping the sync call in asyncio.to_thread, retest with a smaller-but-valid public mp4 (e.g. https://download.samplelib.com/mp4/sample-5s.mp4) — 5 successful uploads should complete in roughly max(t_single), not 5*t_single. Also verify hashtag search still works (currently RUNNING path, not sync/CACHED, since Apify hashtag actor took >25s in this run).

rca_of_the_issue.reported_bug: Cloudflare 502 'invalid or incomplete response' during /api/reels/upload with 10+ reels.
rca_of_the_issue.attempted_fix: routes/reels.py:800-822 — asyncio.gather(*(_bounded(reel) for reel in request.reels)) with Semaphore(5).
rca_of_the_issue.why_fix_is_incomplete: The gathered coroutine upload_reel_to_cloudinary contains a synchronous blocking call `cloudinary.uploader.upload(video_url, ...)` (services/cloudinary_service.py:94). Python's asyncio cannot preempt a sync call; while one coroutine sits in the SDK's blocking HTTP request, the event loop is frozen. So all 10 coroutines run one at a time, exactly as before.
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: POST /api/reels/upload with 5 reels → check backend.err.log Cloudinary error timestamps → observe strictly increasing timestamps ~200-230ms apart, proving serial execution.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: Wrap the SDK call: `result = await asyncio.to_thread(cloudinary.uploader.upload, video_url, resource_type='video', folder=CLOUDINARY_FOLDER, public_id=public_id, overwrite=True)`. This offloads the blocking network I/O to Python's default ThreadPoolExecutor, letting Semaphore(5) genuinely bound 5 concurrent uploads.
